name: PEN
notes: Inclusion note: PEN is a named collaboration at a fixed facility that completed data taking, but no published physics result was found; it is included because the brief names it and PIONEER builds on it. Kind is muon_precision as the nearest kind for a pion-decay experiment.
The PEN web page at galileo.phys.virginia.edu failed certificate verification and was not used.

physics_goals.quote: the PEN collaboration has undertaken a precise measurement of B_{\pi e2} = R^\pi_{e/\mu}, the \pi^+ -> e^+\nu(\gamma) decay branching ratio, at the Paul Scherrer Institute
physics_goals.value: Measure the pi+ -> e+ nu(gamma) branching ratio at PSI to reduce the experimental precision lag behind theory and test lepton universality

summary.plain: An experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute that measured how often a charged pion decays to a positron instead of a muon, a very precise test of whether electrons and muons feel the weak force identically. It took data in 2008-2010; the final result has not been published.
summary.technical: PEN at PSI: precise measurement of the pi+ -> e+ nu(gamma) branching ratio R_e/mu to test lepton universality; over 2 x 10^7 pi_e2 events collected in 2008-2010. The PIONEER experiment builds on PEN and PiENu. No final result found in sources consulted.
